recipes.name: Fruited Curry Chicken Salad
ingredients_raw: 4 skinless, boneless chicken breast halves - cooked and diced
1 small apple - peeled, cored and chopped

steps.text: In a large salad bowl combine the chicken, celery, onion, apple, raisins, grapes, pecans, pepper, curry powder and mayonnaise. Mix all together, tossing to coat. Salad is ready to serve!

raw_recipe.headline: Fruited Curry Chicken Salad
raw_recipe.description: Diced chicken dressed with curry mayonnaise sports a wonderful assortment of apple, raisins and grapes, plus celery, onion and pecans for savory crunch.

review.reviewBody:
This is a variation of a standard popular recipe, and while still good, it can use some tweaking. To thin the mayonnaise, combine with a portion of sour cream or yogurt and maybe even a little lemon juice. Golden raisins and green grapes are a redundancy. Use dark raisins or dried cranberries, or red grapes for color and contrast, and I would prefer red onion or scallions.
Remember to add salt to taste. Enjoy!

EXCELLENT!!!! When my daughter, mother, and I tasted this our eyes rolled back into our heads. It was light and refreshing. I didn't have apples so I just left them out. I substituted walnuts for the pecans and used red grapes instead of green. What a treat to have found this recipe. Thank you so much.

Easy and delicious - plus it's a great way to use up leftover grilled chicken! I didn't have pecans so I subbed toasted walnuts instead. I used a Granny Smith Apple and red seedless grapes vs. green. I also used dried cranberries vs. raisins. I mixed the dressing in a separate bowl before folding it into the chicken and other ingredients. For the dressing I used 1/2 cup of Hellman's light mayo cut with 1/4 cup of reduced fat sour cream along with the curry and a bit of salt and pepper. It chilled for just a couple of hours and it came out really good. Overall, a great combination of flavors! Especially good on whole grain bread!

I replaced half the mayonnaise with yogurt to lessen the caloric impact, and the yogurt complemented the curry wonderfully. I strongly suggest increasing the amount of curry powder, pecans, and celery to add a nice texture as well as making the dish more flavorful. I also used green onions instead of yellow, and salted the salad to taste, as the recipie does not call for any.
After I poached the chicken, I food-processed half of the chicken, and cut the remainder up into small cubes. 
I also recommend using red grapes or dried cherries or raisins, as the finished product was one-note and not very colorful otherwise.

Made it twice both times using rotisserie chickens. If you use rotisserie chicken make sure the pieces are cut up small. Used dark raisins instead of golden ones and it did not impact it much. Great flavors especially left in fridge overnight. I used half a cup of low fat mayo with olive oil and 1/2 cup of low fat Daisy sour cream.Added some fresh squeezed lemon juice (only about 1 TBSP). So incredible yummy!. Both times I made it everyone loved it I served the first version on top of cut up fresh ciabatta half slices but it was hard to keep the salad on top of the bread...Second time I diced the chicken pieces smaller and served it inside croissants. Do not overtoast the pecans...Overall, wonderful mingled flavors!!! Thanks for sharing.

Fabulous!!!! Made tea sandwiches with this for a large ladies luncheon and everyone asked for the recipe. I tweaked alot due to what I had on hand and wanting a NO MAYO recipe as I am allergic; As follows: Subbed sour cream for mayo, and quarter cup minced scallions for onion, used 1/2 C. pomegranate raisins instead of grapes, topped with toasted coconut when assembling sandwiches. Added a good dash garlic salt, 6 T. of curry powder, 1 t. coriander, 1 t. cayenne and 1/2 C. honey. I also added a good dose of salt and some cracked black pepper to taste. This would be lovely served atop leaf lettuce sprinkled w the toasted coconut and flash of toasted almonds for EXTRA crunch.

This is a great tasty recipe. I did it with leftover turkey breast this time and will use chicken next time. Cosmic crisp apple were the flavor bomb in this and craisins and red grapes can be used for more color. Pretty flexible. I used 1/4 Cup Mayo and 1/2 cup Greek yogurt this time but have used just mayonnaise before. Every time I make it we always want more. Made extra for leftovers because it tastes even better the next day. I served it with flatbread and a spinach salad. Would be great for potluck.

Ah! How do I edit my review? I wasn’t finished :( Anyway, I had some leftover shredded chicken that I needed to find something to do with, and I found this recipe and tried it, even though I didn’t have all the ingredients listed. I used shredded chicken, a large green apple, raisins, mayo (then ran out of mayo so added a bit of sour cream), pepper, and a bit of coriander and cumin since I didn’t have curry powder. Let me say, even just these ingredients made this chicken it amazing! I can’t wait to eat my delicious repurposed shredded chicken for lunch over the next two days (I’m getting hungry just thinking about it). Will definitely have to try again with all of the standard ingredients.

I did 2 cans of chickpeas instead of chicken, subbed a bell pepper instead of celery (I don't like celery), and I didn't have pecans. It was pretty amazing fresh, I can't wait to eat it tomorrow when the flavors have mingled!

Excellent dish just the way it's written, but it also can accept many modifications to fit your likes and dislikes. Add more celery/onion/apple/etc or leave them out - whatever you prefer. Same with the curry - if you love it, or have a mild curry in the house, add lots. If your curry is on the strong side, tone it down. Most of the time I cook fresh, but this is one of those dishes that does well with canned chicken. So if it's summertime, no heating up the house and you still have a delicious meal. Make it early in the day, or even the night before so that flavors can blend. Thank you Karen - I make this one regularly.
Family favorite!!

Very tasty! I increased the curry a bit and decided to thinly sliced the apples and layer on roll or greens just under the salad. Was concerned that if there was some leftover, the apple would brown and get too soft and wouldn't be very appealing.
Great! Served it on a bed of lettuce. Yum.

This a fantastic salad! I double the amount of Curry powder and limit the onion to approx 1/3 C. Must make with the grapes and apple. I serve it on a bed of spring greens drizzled with a Ranch dressing to which I add curry powder. Delish! My family loves it.
Made w chicken substitute (vegan) and added a little cayenne pepper. Excellent!!!
Delicious! I used green onions instead of white. Make the day before so flavors can really develop overnight! This recipe is a winner.

Made this for Father's Day picnic, among several other dishes, and this was the one he went crazy over. He's still eating it, now, in front of the T.V.
He doesn't like fruit or nuts in his salads so I left out the raisins, grapes and pecans. I kept in the apple (Honeycrisp) for sweetness and chopped them pretty small so it's hard to tell it's in there. I added about 6X the curry and about 1/4 t ground cloves.
I used the breasts of rotisserie chicken I bought pre-cooked.
I love this recipe! I leave out the grapes and use sliced almonds, because that’s what I usually have on hand.

I love this recipe for an easy meal prep item. I love it over lettuce or on bread but I do only use 2/3 of the mayo called for. Sooo yummy with bursts of sweet, salty, crunchy, and creamy curry deliciousness
